findings.confidence: source-proven timing defect; causal explanation of this run remains runtime-unconfirmed
findings.fact: The fixture's :stall branch sleeps 3000ms before the only peer-close receive. Startup closure polling has 250 sleeps of 10ms, nominally 2500ms plus scheduler/call overhead. A promptly closed client can therefore fail the unchanged test while the fixture is still deliberately asleep.

findings.confidence: source-proven evidence-integrity defect; not independently identified as current failure cause
findings.fact: The old fixture sends :closed unconditionally from its after block. Handshake failure, request timeout, receive timeout and unexpected client bytes can all increment closed after fixture-initiated cleanup. That counter alone does not prove peer EOF.

accepted increments before TLS handshake or HTTP request admission. Passing accepted == 3 establishes transport acceptance only; the third request may have entered handshake, HTTP read, or the stalled-response branch. The old boolean assertion retains none of those stage facts. The candidate acknowledges fixture ownership registration before releasing the handler, eliminating cross-sender accepted/finished ordering as an accounting ambiguity.

findings.confidence: source review only; not product leak clearance
findings.fact: Production BoundedTCP registers the owned raw TCP port before TLS ownership transfer. FetchFlight tracks raw-port and TLS-controller monitors. Graceful flight termination kills the worker, closes raw/TLS sockets, waits for raw port DOWN and controller DOWN, then worker DOWN. KeyOwner termination waits for each flight DOWN. This supplies a concrete cleanup path, but the failing run did not retain the third raw port/controller states or peer EOF.
